description.narrative: Oour Voices Our Futures (OVOF) will use capacity-building and convenings among feminist movements to strengthen and build movements within countries and across regions, while also link feminist movements to relevant actors, such as internet rights’ movements, Dutch allies and progressive policymakers. OVOF believes in strengthening movements from within, to create more inclusive, powerful and resilient movements. To influence laws and policies at national and international levels, OVOF sees this as the only sustainable mitigation strategy in relation to the increasing power of anti-rights and anti-gender forces.

This collective framework positioned Sudanese feminists within global and regional movements thereby forging cross border solidarity.

CREA with its local partners aims to organise 4 collective actions/initiatives in Sudan.

CREA partner in Sudan successfully brought together 15 diverse participants as part of the first cohort of the Feminist Transformative Leadership Training that took place in April. This group included 6 LBTQ individuals, 5 feminist activists, and 4 Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs), each bringing unique perspectives and experiences. Throughout the program, five skilled facilitators led interactive sessions that explored critical themes related to feminist leadership, advocacy, and community-building. The training provided participants with practical tools, knowledge, and a supportive environment to strengthen their roles as advocates and leaders in their communities.

OVOF partners succesfully established (a) a feminist hub with Sudanese feminists in exile which offers a secure environment for activists, students, researchers, and marginalized groups (including LGBTQ+ individuals) to reflect, study and use of short stays, and heal, (b) established a library with a collection focused on Sudanese history, feminist theory, women’s movements, post-colonial studies, and social sciences, tailored to meet the needs of displaced researchers, students, and activists. The library is accessible for reading and borrowing, providing critical intellectual resources to support learning, research, and advocacy in exile.
